copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Wednesday, evening UTC kickoff, brings England and Croatia together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Croatia side, by +8.2pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Public Elo rates England 90 points higher than the other side (England 1950, Croatia 1860). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: England to win at 47%, the draw at 25%, and Croatia to win at 28%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Croatia on the win side reads 28%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: England to win at 55%, the draw at 22%, and Croatia to win at 20%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Croatia side — 20% on the market, 28% on the engine, a +8.2pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Croatia side that lower bound is 24% — +3.8pp clear of the market's 20%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Croatia side.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 26 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page. Per BBC Sport (football): "Foden and Palmer to miss out on World Cup squad" The Guardian (football) carried the same line: "handing a surprise recall to Ivan Toney"
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Croatia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +8.2pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

copy.summary: This is a Pick on the Croatia side — the model has them at 28%, the market at 20%. A +8.2pp gap is enough on a fixture this close to even.
